title: Isolation of Total RNA from Mouse Cochlea Using Organic Solvents
author: Rías, Spitzmaul, et al.
materials: Pestle for 1.5 mL Micro Centrifuge Tube
1.5 mL Micro Centrifuge Tube RNAse/DNAse free

steps.title: Prepare reagents (day before)
steps.instruction: Store 1X PBS at 4 °C (homemade preparation with ultrapure water is acceptable). Place a frozen 7 cm‑diameter petri dish in a freezer to serve as a cooling base for dissection. Prepare 70 % ethanol by mixing ultrapure water (PB‑L Productos Bio‑Lógicos, cat N° IA0602) with absolute ethanol (J. T. Baker) and store the ethanol at –20 °C.

steps.title: Set up ice‑cold PBS and clean workspace
steps.instruction: Prepare 500 mL of 1X PBS and keep it on ice. Clean all working surfaces with 70 % ethanol. Dispense ice‑cold PBS into a 35 mm cell‑culture dish and keep the dish on ice for the upcoming dissection.

steps.title: Euthanize mouse and expose temporal bone
steps.instruction: Euthanize the mouse in a CO₂ chamber or by decapitation (cervical dislocation is not recommended). Using No. 5 surgical scissors, remove skin and connective tissue around the skull. Cut off the anterior snout region, then make a midline incision from the foramen magnum rostrally to expose the cranial cavity. Using No. 5 forceps, remove the cranial bone over each hemisphere to reveal the brain, then remove the brain with a spatula. With fine scissors, sever the nerves linking the ear to the brainstem. Isolate the temporal bone, position it ventral side up, open the tympanic bulla to expose the middle‑ear cavity, rotate laterally to view the semicircular canals, cut along natural bone fissures with micro‑scissors, trim excess bone while avoiding pressure on the cochlea, gently release lateral connective attachments with fine forceps, and lift the inner ear from the temporal bone.

steps.title: Dissect cochlea from inner ear
steps.instruction: Transfer both inner ears into the ice‑cold PBS dish under a stereomicroscope. Using fine‑tipped forceps (No. 5, Dumont 11254‑20), remove all tissue surrounding the otic capsule. Open the auditory bulla with iris scissors (No. 5, cat 14060‑09) to create a small fracture along thinner regions, gently widen the opening to expose the cochlea, and remove the intact inner ear from the bulla with minimal disruption. With the same iris scissors, excise the vestibular apparatus and isolate the cochlea.

steps.title: Snap‑freeze cochleae
steps.instruction: Place each cochlea into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube and immediately snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen for 10 seconds. Store the tubes at –20 °C while dissecting the next mouse. Wear insulated gloves, safety goggles, face shield, closed‑top shoes, long pants and long‑sleeved shirts when handling liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Process additional mice and pool samples
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 3–5 for the second mouse: after snap‑freezing, add the second cochlea to the same tube containing the first mouse’s cochlea, and store at –20 °C. For the third mouse, add its cochlea to the same tube (resulting in three cochleae per 1.5 mL tube) or, alternatively, place the third cochlea in a new tube and then pool three cochleae per tube as indicated. Ensure each tube contains exactly three cochleae to obtain sufficient RNA yield.

description: This protocol is adapted from the classical organic solvent-based RNA extraction method described by Chomczynski and Sacchi (1987).2 It has been optimized to obtain high-quality total RNA from mice cochleae, with yields and purity suitable for downstream molecular analyses such as reverse transcription and quantitative PCR. We have successfully used this procedure to assess gene expression in different cochlear components under both normal and pathological conditions (Rías et al., 2025).1 The day before to cochleae dissection:1.Store 1X PBS at 4°C.Note: A homemade 1X PBS solution prepared with ultrapure water can be used.2.Place a cooling device to use as a base for cochlear dissection in the freezer. A frozen petri dish of 7 cm diameter could be used for this purpose.3.Prepare 70% ethanol using ultrapure water (PB-L Productos Bio-Lógicos, cat N° IA0602) and high-quality absolute ethanol (J. T. Baker). Store at −20°C.
